title: Map Insert and Get
story: You're building a translation app. Users type 'hello' and expect 'hola'. You need to store word pairs and look them up instantly. But what if a user types a word you don't know? Your app needs to handle that gracefully.
why: `.insert()` stores data and handles overwrites; `.get()` retrieves it safely with `Option` — together they form the read/write cycle of any key-value store.
analogy: `.insert()` and `.get()` are like a library's card catalog. You file a card under a title (insert key→value). Later, you look up that title (get) and instantly find the book's location. If you file a NEW card under the same title, it replaces the old one — the catalog always has the latest info.
try_it: Build a translation dictionary with 5 word pairs. Write a `translate` function that returns the translation or '???' if unknown. Add a `update_or_insert` function that only inserts if the key doesn't exist yet. What happens if you insert different value types (like trying to insert a Str into a Map[Str,Int])?
tips: `.insert()` overwrites without warning — use `.contains()` first if you need to check before replacing
`.get()` returns the value wrapped in Option — match on `Some` for success, `None` for missing keys
Store related values under meaningful keys — `"product_name"` is better than `"key1"`
common_mistakes: Assuming `.insert()` adds a duplicate — it overwrites, so the Map always has exactly one value per key
Not handling the `None` case from `.get()` — keys might not exist, and your program shouldn't crash
Using `.get()` with the wrong key type — the key must match the Map's K type parameter
